newsitem.title: CHINA: 150,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat in ships off China.
newsitem.headline: 150,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat in ships off China.

text.p: A total of about 150,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat tainted by a fungus known as TCK smut is sitting in ships off the Chinese ports of Shanghai and Fuzhou, an official of the U.S. Agricultural Trade Office said on Wednesday.
He said about 100,000 tonnes are in two ships off Shanghai and 50,000 tonnes in one ship off Fuzhou, he said.
The ships arrived in August and the U.S. has sent scientific experts to look into the problem, he said.
Asked who was paying for the ships as they waited, the official said he believed it was a local trading company, but had no more details.
Beijing and Washington have argued for years over the TCK smut issue. China refuses to allow entry of wheat tainted by the fungus while the U.S. says it poses no risk to Chinese wheat.
An official of the Shanghai branch of Ceroils said there was U.S. wheat tainted by the fungus both in Shanghai and in Guangzhou port but declined to gave details.
An official of the Shanghai Animal and Plant Quarantine Bureau said the issue needed to be settled at the national level. He declined further comment.
